checks: Source digest matches the original note. Section 1 and (3)–(4) support the same fixed N, positive full-dimensional fibers, continuous unit normals, finite threshold saturation, and inball bound.

The contribution of one cap and fiber is at least |K_z|(-R-t_iz)_+ by the unit normal. Since all summands are nonnegative and total hinge is bounded by B, each threshold is bounded below by -R-B/|K_z|. This excludes precisely negative divergence.

Use the common ball and successive subsequences for finitely many cap indices. Previously selected mass limits and the fixed-point membership implication persist on a further subsequence. Each point has some repeated cap index on the final subsequence, independently of whether different points use different indices.

Finite limiting thresholds are reproduced exactly by the predecessor's construction; thresholds diverging positively are realized above R. Unit normals stay unit, and the finite affine threshold has the required form b_i-a_i·z. Hinge convergence is uniform on each finite-threshold fiber by the 1-Lipschitz positive part, and both hinges vanish eventually on the positively divergent fibers.

Integrating the inball slice in the unit direction and substituting s=r_z²-t² gives κ_(d-1) r_z^(d+1)/(d+1). In d=1 this is the direct integral r_z²/2. The chosen cap covers the inball center and therefore has at least this hinge contribution, and summing uses one separate fiber term per base.
